key_insight: MethylVI is a deep probabilistic generative model tailored to single-cell bisulfite sequencing data that explicitly models technical noise and biological variation to produce denoised, imputed, and biologically meaningful methylation profiles.
problem_solved: Single-cell bisulfite sequencing data are extremely sparse, noisy, and subject to coverage and batch biases, making reliable methylation quantification, imputation, and downstream analysis (clustering, integration) difficult.
method: Probabilistic deep generative model (VAE-style) that learns a low‑dimensional latent representation of cells capturing biological signal.
Explicit noise/observation model for per-site/per-cell methylation measurements and sequencing coverage to separate technical variability from biology.
Uses the learned latent space for denoising, imputing missing CpG methylation values, batch correction, and improved downstream analyses.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a principled way to model sparse methylation counts and extract robust latent features for classification, integration, and generative tasks, improving downstream analysis and reproducibility in single‑cell epigenomics.
visual_elements: Model schematic: encoder→latent space→decoder with an overlay showing the probabilistic observation model for methylation and coverage.
Heatmap before vs. after denoising/imputation of methylation matrix to show sparsity reduction and signal recovery.
Latent-space UMAP colored by cell type and batch to illustrate biological separation and batch correction.
Bar/line chart comparing imputation accuracy or downstream clustering metrics (with and without MethylVI).
paper_title: Probabilistic modelling of single-cell bisulfite sequencing data with MethylVI
paper_authors: Ethan Weinberger, Wei Qiu, Wei Tian, Qiurui Zeng, Can Ergen
